newsitem.title: USA: SANTA FE INT'L SEES FURTHER IMPROVEMENT.
newsitem.headline: SANTA FE INT'L SEES FURTHER IMPROVEMENT.

text.p: Santa Fe International Corp said Friday higher day-rates for its offshore rigs helped the company acheive a substantial improvement earnings for the year and fourth quarter, adding it expects favorable market conditions to continue to improve its operating results.

"With the existing strong market conditions, we expect continued growth for the company and further improvements in our operating results," said Sted Garber, the company's chief operating officer, in a statement accompanying fourth quarter earnings.
Net income for the fourth quarter rose to $53.3 million, or $0.47 per share, from $21.5 million or $0.19 per share a year ago, the company said.
The company reported a 166 percent increase in full year 1997 net income to $164.9 million, or $1.44 per share.
Analysts had been looking for fourth quarter earnings per share of $0.43, according to First Call, which included two analysts its survey.

The company said average daily revenue for the 26 rig marine fleet was $49,100 in the fourth quarter of its year which ended June 30, and $42,600 for the full fiscal year, up from $34,200 and $32,400, respectively.
Average offshore rig utilization rose to 100 percent in the fourth quarter and 95.5 percent in the year from 89.6 percent and 88.8 percent.
Its land rig day-rates rose to $14,100 and $13,100 respectively from $11,800 and $12,300.
"Market demand has enabled us to increase rig utilization. We have also been able to increase our day-rates at contract rollover," Gerber said.
He said that the company has begun building a harsh operating environment jack-up rig which will begin a five year contract when it is completed in the fourth quarter of 1998.
Santa Fe shares were trading off 1/8 at 41-1/8 after the earnings announcement.
